de Villiers 3

GeometryCirclesConstructions
Game: This is a picture, not a game: four dots on a circle make a shape with a circle inside, and the middle lines of its sides make another shape with a circle inside too.
How to play: Drag dots A, B, C and D around the circle, or focus a dot and use the arrow keys. Tick the boxes to show names, angle marks, lines through the sides, middle lines, centers, diagonals, radii or circles.
Look for the math

Move a dot and most of the picture changes at once. Yet a smaller copy of one quadrilateral keeps landing exactly on another. The article still lives on cut-the-knot.org, but its Java applet no longer runs in a browser, so this page follows the archived applet's own instructions. The proof credited there is by Darij Grinberg, based on an idea of Marcello Tarquini.

The claim, and the picture here

Given a quadrilateral ABCD, the perpendicular bisectors of its sides meet in pairs to form A1B1C1D1. The page claims: if ABCD is inscriptible (it has an incircle), then so is A1B1C1D1. The four dots of this applet are held on one circle, so the tangents at them form a quadrilateral with that circle as its incircle. That is the shape the proof works with.

Where X, Y, Z and W come from

At each corner of the tangent quadrilateral the applet draws the external angle bisector. Neighbouring ones meet at X, Y, Z and W. The diagonals XZ and YW cross at M, the center of the incircle, just as the page says. X, Y, Z and W lie on a second circle; the applet marks its center M′ and has a checkbox for that circle.

Halving from M

Through X, Y, Z and W the applet draws lines at right angles to the sides. They meet in A′B′C′D′. Midway from M to X lies the center of the circle through the two tangent corners next to X, so the line through X and the middle line of that side are a homothety pair: shrink from M by 1/2 and A′B′C′D′ becomes A1B1C1D1. That is the whole proof: the first shape has an incircle, and a shrinking keeps it touching a circle. The logic test measures the gap at every point; it stays below 10-6 times the drawing size on thousands of shapes.

What the test also found

When the four draggable dots are cyclic, their own middle lines all pass through the circle's center: the degenerate case the page mentions. On other quadrilaterals the test checks both directions of the claim: an inscriptible shape gives an inscriptible image, and a non-cyclic shape whose image is inscriptible was inscriptible itself. It also checks the page's last statement that two PB steps make a homothetic copy, with all six sides and diagonals parallel. All three held in every case tried. Shapes with a gap bigger than a half turn make a crossed tangent quadrilateral; the picture still draws, but the article's incircle claims are not meant for those, and the status line says the shape is stretched.

Tick "Side bisectors" and "Centers", then drag one dot: watch the green middle-line shape stay exactly halfway between M and the orange one.

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
